prompt: A message crosses three equal-rate, initially idle store-and-forward links. It is split into several packets; ignore the added header overhead. Why can the split message finish sooner than one large packet?

options.text: The first packet skips transmission on later links
options.explanation: Each packet must still be transmitted on every link.

options.text: Each router forwards before receiving a complete packet
options.explanation: That would be cut-through; the question specifies store-and-forward.

options.text: Different links can transmit different complete packets at the same time
options.explanation: Correct. Once the first packet reaches the next router, one link can send it onward while the previous link handles a later packet.

options.text: Several packets transmit simultaneously on the same serial link
options.explanation: A serial link handles them in sequence; the useful overlap is across different links.

workedExample: Follow the first packet: it must be received completely at each router before going onward. While it crosses the second link, the sender can put the next packet on the first link. That overlap fills the pipeline. Extra per-packet headers can offset the benefit if packets are made too small.
